## Research question
How does Ridgeline-FT compare with Plainweave-FT in pass@1 on Quillbench?

## Methods summary
Ridgeline-FT fine-tunes a code model with an execution-feedback curriculum that orders training problems by the failure rate of the model's own samples. Plainweave-FT is standard supervised fine-tuning on the same data. Both start from the same 1.3B-parameter base model, Fernleaf-1.3B, which is also reported without fine-tuning.

## Experimental setup
Both recipes fine-tune Fernleaf-1.3B on the same 85,000 problem–solution pairs, each with 8 random seeds (seeds 0–7); seed i fixes data order and initialization for both recipes, so seed-level scores are paired. Evaluation uses greedy decoding on all 420 Quillbench problems (Python, hidden unit tests). The analysis plan pre-specified two endpoints for Ridgeline-FT vs Plainweave-FT, pass@1 (primary) and compile rate (secondary), and controls the family-wise error rate across these two tests with the Holm–Bonferroni procedure at α = 0.05.

## Experiments and comparisons
- `exp1`: Ridgeline-FT vs Plainweave-FT on Quillbench (420 problems)
  - comparison `exp1/cmp1`: Ridgeline-FT vs Plainweave-FT, pass@1 (primary endpoint)
  - comparison `exp1/cmp2`: Ridgeline-FT vs Plainweave-FT, compile rate (secondary endpoint)

## Results tables
### Table T1: Quillbench results, mean ± SD over 8 seeds (base model: single deterministic run).
Columns: `pass1` = pass@1 (%) [unit: %] (higher is better); `compile` = Compile rate (%) [unit: %] (higher is better)
| row_id | label | pass1 | compile |
|---|---|---|---|
| r1 | Ridgeline-FT (ours) | 46.1 ± 1.8 | 93.1 ± 1.3 |
| r2 | Plainweave-FT | 45.6 ± 1.7 | 90.4 ± 1.8 |
| r3 | Fernleaf-1.3B (no fine-tuning) | 31.4 | 84.0 |

## Statistical tests
- `S1` for comparison `exp1/cmp1`: paired t-test; two-sided; paired; n=8 random seeds (paired by seed); t=0.97 (df=7); Holm-adjusted p = 0.36; 95% CI [-0.75, 1.79] for mean paired difference in pass@1 (Ridgeline-FT − Plainweave-FT), percentage points; unadjusted 95% CI; alpha=0.05; adjustment: Holm–Bonferroni across the two pre-specified endpoints (S1 pass@1, S2 compile rate); note: Unadjusted p = 0.36 (unchanged by the Holm step-down).
- `S2` for comparison `exp1/cmp2`: paired t-test; two-sided; paired; n=8 random seeds (paired by seed); t=4.14 (df=7); Holm-adjusted p = 0.0087; 95% CI [1.19, 4.35] for mean paired difference in compile rate (Ridgeline-FT − Plainweave-FT), percentage points; unadjusted 95% CI; alpha=0.05; adjustment: Holm–Bonferroni across the two pre-specified endpoints (S1 pass@1, S2 compile rate); note: Unadjusted p = 0.0043.

## Task

sentences.text: On Quillbench, Ridgeline-FT achieved a mean pass@1 of 46.1% ± 1.8% compared with 45.6% ± 1.7% for Plainweave-FT, a difference that was not statistically significant (paired t-test, Holm-adjusted p = 0.36).

Ridgeline-FT showed a significantly higher compile rate than Plainweave-FT (93.1% ± 1.3% vs. 90.4% ± 1.8%; mean paired difference 2.77 percentage points, 95% CI [1.19, 4.35], Holm-adjusted p = 0.0087).
Thus, the evidence supports a benefit of Ridgeline-FT over Plainweave-FT in compile rate but not in pass@1 on this benchmark.

On Quillbench, Ridgeline-FT achieved a mean pass@1 of 46.1% ± 1.8% compared with 45.6% ± 1.7% for Plainweave-FT, a difference that was not statistically significant (paired t-test, Holm-adjusted p = 0.36).

Ridgeline-FT had a significantly higher mean compile rate than Plainweave-FT (93.1% ± 1.3% vs. 90.4% ± 1.8%; mean paired difference (Ridgeline−Plainweave) 2.77 percentage points, 95% CI [1.19, 4.35], Holm-adjusted p = 0.0087, secondary endpoint).
Both fine-tuned variants substantially outperformed the base model Fernleaf-1.3B (31.4% pass@1, 84.0% compile).
On Quillbench, Ridgeline-FT did not significantly differ from Plainweave-FT in pass@1 (46.1% ± 1.8% vs 45.6% ± 1.7%; paired t-test, Holm-adjusted p = 0.36, 95% CI [-0.75, 1.79] percentage points).
However, Ridgeline-FT significantly outperformed Plainweave-FT in compile rate (93.1% ± 1.3% vs 90.4% ± 1.8%; paired t-test, Holm-adjusted p = 0.0087, 95% CI [1.19, 4.35] percentage points).
Both fine-tuned recipes improved pass@1 and compile rate over the base Fernleaf-1.3B model (pass@1: 46.1% and 45.6% vs 31.4%; compile: 93.1% and 90.4% vs 84.0%).
